"Build something real. Ship it in a week.                                    
   ​AgnesCode Build Challenge is a solo, online hackathon where you build       
   anything you want using AgnesCode, Agnes AI's agentic coding tool. Games,    
   apps, tools, automations, research assistants. If you can build it with an AI
    coding agent, it's fair game.                                               
                                                                                
   ​What is AgnesCode?                                                          
   AgnesCode is Agnes AI's agentic coding tool, similar to Claude Code or Codex.
    It lets you build full projects through natural language, with Agnes AI     
   models doing the heavy lifting. Agnes 2.0 Flash and Agnes 2.5 Flash are      
   completely free to use inside AgnesCode.                                     
                                                                                
   ​Who can join                                                                
   Anyone. All skill levels welcome. You do not need to be a professional       
   developer. This is open to builders, students, hobbyists, and developers     
   alike. First 50 registrants are eligible so register early.                  
                                                                                
   ​Requirements to participate                                                 
   Before submitting you must have an Agnes AI account, have AgnesCode          
   installed, be a member of the Agnes AI Discord server (                      
   Join Discord Server                                                          
   ), and be following Agnes AI on X (                                          
   /                                                                            
   agnesai_sapiens                                                              
   ).                                                                           
                                                                                
   ​Tracks                                                                      
   When submitting you will choose one track for your project. Judges score     
   within each track's context, not against other tracks.                       
                                                                                
   ​AI in Product: apps, tools, or websites people can actually use             
                                                                                
   ​AI in Automation and Infrastructure: workflows, scripts, deployment helpers, 
   dev tools                                                                    
                                                                                
   ​AI in Creativity: games, generative art, creative tools, interactive        
   experiences                                                                  
                                                                                
   ​AI in Research and Learning: research assistants, study tools, knowledge    
   systems, educational apps                                                    
                                                                                
   ​How it works                                                                
   Register on this page before the cap hits 50. Once the build week opens on   
   Aug 20, start building your project using AgnesCode with Agnes 2.0 Flash or  
   Agnes 2.5 Flash. Projects must be started during the build week, pre-built   
   projects are not allowed. Push your work to a public GitHub repository,      
   record a short demo video, and submit before Aug 26 11:30 PM SGT. The        
   submission form will be shared on the Agnes AI Discord server when the build 
   week begins. Make sure you are in the server and following #hackathon-chat so
    you do not miss it.                                                         
                                                                                
   ​What to submit                                                              
                                                                                
   ​Public GitHub repository link (must be public at time of submission)        
                                                                                
   ​YouTube unlisted demo video, 2 to 3 minutes maximum, must show the project  
   actually running                                                             
                                                                                
   ​AgnesCode diagnostics file exported from the app as proof of Agnes model    
   usage                                                                        
                                                                                
   ​Project description covering what you built, who it is for, what problem it 
   solves or what experience it creates, and key technical decisions you made. A
    few solid paragraphs, not a one-liner.                                      
                                                                                
   ​Short answers on what your project does well, where it breaks or falls short,
    and what you would build next with two more weeks                           
                                                                                
   ​How projects are judged                                                     
   3 judges will independently score each valid submission across 5 pillars and 
   scores will be averaged. Each pillar is scored 1 to 5 for a maximum total of 
   25 points.                                                                   
                                                                                
   ​Problem or Purpose: why does this project exist and what would success look 
   like?                                                                        
                                                                                
   ​Approach and Use of AgnesCode: did you use the agent thoughtfully and       
   meaningfully?                                                                
                                                                                
   ​Evidence it Works: does the project actually function based on the repo and 
   demo?                                                                        
                                                                                
   ​Constraints and Honesty: do you know what you built and where it breaks?    
                                                                                
   ​Creativity or Impact: is it interesting or useful beyond the hackathon      
   context?                                                                     
                                                                                
   ​The guiding principle for judges is that a modest claim proven beats a grand 
   claim asserted. Polish alone does not win.                                   
                                                                                
   ​Prizes                                                                      
                                                                                
   ​1st place: AgnesCode Pro, 1 month ($100 value)                              
                                                                                
   ​2nd place: AgnesCode Plus, 1 month ($20 value)                              
                                                                                
   ​3rd place: AgnesCode Plus, 1 month ($20 value)                              
                                                                                
   ​Disqualification                                                            
   Submissions will be automatically disqualified if the diagnostics file is    
   missing or shows no Agnes model usage, the GitHub repository is private or   
   missing, the demo video is missing or does not show the project running, or  
   the registration requirements were not completed before submitting. "

   I run an autonomous poker agent that has made thousands of real-money        
   decisions on DevFun Arena (Monad). It runs unattended: it joins seasons,     
   buys rebuys, plays hands, and manages its own bankroll. The problem this     
   project solves is that nobody checks whether such an agent is still the      
   agent it claims to be. Its own advisory loop quietly rotted while looking    
   busy: 6,243 shadow-LLM policy suggestions generated, 6 promoted. That is a   
   system you cannot assertEquals.                                              
                                                                                
   sekats ("stakes", reversed) is the human quality layer for that agent. It    
   turns the agent's own strategy manual (poker-policy.json) into checkable     
   acceptance criteria, surfaces where its automated review pipeline disagrees  
   with its actual decisions, and gives a human a real queue to adjudicate      
   those disagreements instead of trusting a dashboard that says everything is  
   fine.                                                                        
                                                                                
   The core numbers are computed by code, never by a model. The shadow-LLM      
   review pipeline currently agrees with the agent's actual decisions on only   
   84.3% of linked reviews (1,497/1,775), with a repeatable failure pattern:    
   the agent bets marginal spots where the shadow reviewer says check. Sekats   
   links every review to the exact decision row that triggered it (a fix after  
   an early table-level join contaminated analysis at ~75x), scores the live    
   policy against those linked outcomes, and streams the disagreements into a   
   human adjudication queue. The LLM in this system narrates; deterministic     
   rules decide.                                                                
                                                                                
   Who it is for: anyone running long-lived autonomous agents — trading bots,   
   ops agents, game-playing agents — who needs to answer "is it still doing     
   what I approved?" after weeks unattended.

# sekats

**stakes**, reversed — a parlor that watches whether a poker agent on
[DevFun Arena](https://arena.dev.fun/) is still the agent it claims to be.

The live runner is the *subject*. This repo is the *check*: a local QC cockpit
plus Kane CLI that treat `arena.dev.fun` as source of truth for anything the
world can see. Kane does not play poker. The probe uses **no API key**.

**Live:** https://sekats.thisyearnofear.com  
(Local: `python3 tools/qc_server.py` → http://127.0.0.1:8765/)

## Routes

| Path | What |
|------|------|

| `/check` | Paste any public agent (URL, id, or live name). Field scan, or pin claimed season ids for **HOLD** / **DRIFT**. |

## Run

Local:

```
python3 tools/qc_server.py
```

Open http://127.0.0.1:8765/ — or use the live parlor above.

```
./verify.sh
```

Runs the Kane `_test.md` suite (needs `kane-cli` + Chrome and the cockpit
listening), then the season probe. Probe exit 1 on **DRIFT** until
`assets/contract.json` matches live `list-active`.

Demo the closed loop:

```

./tools/demo_contract.sh live    # Public → HOLD  (leave it live after)
```

Reload `/sheet` → Public after swapping.

Any-agent (CLI):

```
python3 tools/qc_server.py --probe-only --agent <id-or-name>
python3 tools/qc_server.py --probe-only --agent <id> --claimed <id,id>
```

```
assets/                 # parlor UI + contract.json (+ stale/live for the tape)
```

Hooks block private keys / secrets (gitleaks), fix trailing whitespace, and
lint/format the Python probe (ruff).
